title: The Master Map: Upper vs. Lower Eyelid Reconstruction
summary: A comprehensive guide to adnexal reconstruction, focusing on the lamellar principles, surgical algorithms, and anatomical nuances that differentiate upper lid mobility from lower lid stability.

sections.title: The Fundamental Rule of Lamellae
content: The Eyelid = Anterior Lamella (Skin/Orbicularis) + Posterior Lamella (Tarsus/Conjunctiva).
CRITICAL: You MUST provide a blood supply to at least one lamella. Never place a free graft on another free graft.
Upper Lid Priority: Dynamics and mobility (levator function).
Lower Lid Priority: Stability and support (preventing ectropion/retraction).

rows: Static; acts as a reservoir for tears and support
Prone to horizontal laxity with age

sections.title: Management of Lower Lid Defects
content: Step 1: Assess horizontal laxity and defect width.
Step 2: <33% width -> Primary pentagonal excision and closure in layers (6-0 vicryl tarsus, 6-0 silk margin).
Step 3: 33-50% width -> Lateral canthotomy and inferior cantholysis (adds 2-5mm) OR Tenzel Semicircular Flap.
Step 4: >50% width -> Hughes Tarsoconjunctival Flap (replaces post. lamella) + Skin Graft/Flap (ant. lamella).
Step 5: Total Defect -> Mustardé Rotation Flap (requires large cheek rotation).

sections.title: The Hughes Flap (Lower Lid)
content: Used for large lower lid defects (>50%).
Posterior lamella donor: Tarsus from the ipsilateral UPPER lid.
Crucial: Leave 4mm of tarsus at upper lid margin to prevent entropion.
Second Stage: Pedicle division at 3-4 weeks once vascularized.
Anterior lamella: Must be covered with a full-thickness skin graft (FTSG) or advancement flap.

sections.title: Management of Upper Lid Defects
content: Step 1: Check Levator function and defect size.
Step 2: <33% -> Primary closure (careful margin alignment to prevent notch).
Step 3: 33-50% -> Tenzel flap (superiorly based) or Lateral Cantholysis.
Step 4: >50% -> Cutler-Beard Bridge Flap (lower lid full thickness tissue used).
Step 5: Alternative -> Modified Hughes (Upper) using lower lid tarsus (rare) or Fricke Flap (brow skin).

sections.title: Cutler-Beard Bridge Flap
content: Used for large upper lid defects.
Lower lid tissue is passed 'under' a 4mm bridge of the lower lid margin (to preserve marginal artery).
Full thickness flap (skin, muscle, conjunctiva) but lacks tarsus.
Staged: Flap divided at 4-6 weeks.
Risk: Upper lid stability issues due to lack of tarsal plate (often reinforced with ear cartilage).

content.explanation: Skin, Orbicularis, Septum (Anterior) | Tarsus, Conjunctiva (Posterior). Remembering the Septum separates the 'pre-septal' from 'orbital' compartments.

sections.title: Primary Margin Closure Steps
content: 1. Vertical 'Pentagonal' excision to prevent buckling.
2. 6-0 Vicryl/Dexon through tarsal plate (lamellar depth).
3. 6-0 Silk 'Vertical Mattress' at the Meibomian Gland orifices.
4. 6-0 Silk at the Lash Line (to provide eversion).
5. Leave sutures long and bolster under skin sutures to avoid corneal abrasion.

sections.title: Complications & Red Flags
content: Lid Notching: Failure to align the tarsal plate/gray line correctly.
Trichiasis: Inward turning lashes from poor margin apposition.
Symblepharon: Conjunctival adhesions in the fornix.
Lagophthalmos: Excessive skin resection in upper lid recon.
Ectropion: Gravity and lack of horizontal support in lower lid recon.

sections.title: Pearls for the Oculoplastic Surgeon
content: The 'Lid Tension' test: If the lid doesn't snap back after pulling it 8mm from the globe, perform a lateral tarsal strip.
Medial Defects: Always consider the lacrimal drainage system. Intubate with Crawford tubes if canaliculi are involved.
FTSG Sources: Post-auricular (best match for eyelid), Upper lid (if contralateral skin is redundant), or Supraclavicular.
Mustardé Flap: Requires wide undermining of the cheek down to the periosteum to ensure tension-free closure.

sections.title: Landmark Studies: The ETDRS & BCSC Guidance
sections.content: Modern eyelid reconstruction emphasizes 'Like-for-Like' replacement. The use of Acellular Dermal Matrix (AlloDerm) as a posterior lamella substitute has gained traction in patients who cannot tolerate a staged Hughes flap (e.g., monocular patients). Evidence suggests that maintaining a stable horizontal lid tension is more critical for corneal health than perfect lash alignment.

sections.title: Surgical Instrument Checklist
content: Bishop-Harmon/Paufique Forceps (for delicate skin)
Castroviejo Needle Holder (for 6-0 and 7-0 sutures)
Westcott Scissors (for undermining/dissection)
Desmarres Lid Retractor
Jaeger Lid Plate (to protect globe during incision)
